neighbours.label: words for calcium-carbonate and calcium-sulfate minerals and the soils they make (chalk, calcareous, gypsum, limestone, calcite), as against other rocks and minerals
fire: Along the coast the land rises into tall chalk cliffs above the beach.
Most fields in the valley lie on calcareous clay that drains slowly.
The quarry has produced gypsum for wallboard since the 1950s.
Botanists surveyed the calcareous grassland on the southern slope.
Underneath the topsoil is a thick bed of chalk full of flint.
The rock contains calcite crystals that glow under ultraviolet light.
Farmers spread crushed gypsum to loosen the heavy soil.
The downs are rolling chalk hills covered in short turf.
quiet: Along the coast the land rises into tall granite cliffs above the beach.
Most fields in the valley lie on heavy clay that drains slowly.
The quarry has produced slate for roofing since the 1950s.
Botanists surveyed the acidic grassland on the southern slope.
Underneath the topsoil is a thick bed of gravel full of pebbles.
The rock contains quartz crystals that sparkle in the sunlight.
Farmers spread crushed bark to loosen the heavy soil.
The moors are rolling peat hills covered in heather.
